extracted.intended_audience: Congress, USPTO stakeholders, patent & trademark applicants, and USPTO management
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the USPTO's FY1999 organizational goals, performance measures, targets, and operational standards for patent and trademark processing and service delivery. Covers cycle-time targets, electronic filing requirements, quality measures, customer satisfaction drivers, staffing and fee policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four Business Goals (Patent Business)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish four business goals to provide customers with high-quality service to facilitate issuing of patents in a timely and consistent manner: Goal 1 reduce processing time; Goal 2 receive applications and publish patents electronically; Goal 3 exceed customers' quality expectations through competencies and empowerment of employees; Goal 4 assess fees commensurate with resource use and customer efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each goal is an organizational standard driving initiatives (hiring, electronic systems, quality programs, fee adjustments) and tied to measurable targets and timelines described elsewhere in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal 1: Reduce the PTO processing time
rubrics_metrics.description: By 2003, reduce processing (cycle) time for original UPR inventions to 12 months from receipt of application to patent issue or abandonment. FY1999 target processing time was 10.9 months (actual average cycle time was 12.9 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track component cycle times (time to first action, time from first action to allowance/abandonment, allowance to publication). Use hiring (examiners), cycle time awards, process changes (hiring, training, technical support personnel relieving examiners of non-processing work) to meet targets. Example improvements: response time to amendment reduced from 58 to 54 days during FY1999.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent cycle-time component measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor and manage subcomponents of overall cycle time: cycle time to first action, cycle time from first action to allowance/abandonment, and cycle time from allowance to publication (printing/issuance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets and actuals are reported (e.g., FY1998 cycle time 16.9 months; FY1999 average 12.9 months). Identify and remediate stage(s) causing delays (e.g., missed target for allowance-to-publication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent printing/patent issue turnaround
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue patents and print them in a timely manner so patents can be issued within five weeks after issue fee payment (target).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY1999 required printing 183,000 patents to reduce backlog; actual printing capacity shortfall resulted in patents issued within 16 weeks after issue fee payment. Remedy via publishing process improvements and contractor requirements to meet five-week goal in subsequent fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Initial Patent Examination (OIPE) timeliness standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Mail filing receipts within less than 30 days (average performance target), and reduce time to process and forward patent applications to examination (target example: reduced from 70 days in Oct 1998 to 21 days in Sep 1999).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement quality improvement strategies (databases to track requests for corrected filing receipts by error type), encourage employee ownership and accountability, and implement improved quality sampling; track error reduction (e.g., errors down 26% Feb–Aug 1999).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cycle-time awards and employee incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish cycle time awards as employee incentives for each area of patent processing to motivate reductions in processing time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use awards to drive measurable improvements in specific processing steps (example: amendment response time reduction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal 2: Receive applications and publish patents electronically
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete systems testing and begin full electronic processing of patent applications by FY2003; implement the Electronic Filing System (EFS) and related components (ePAVE, EFS BIO, pilot programs, eventual full EFS production).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFS requirements: applicants obtain digital certificates and public/private keys; transmission security via Public Key Infrastructure; files combine into a single compressed and digitally signed encrypted file; files received in Electronic Mailroom. Implement pilots (biological sequence listings, limited-complexity utility applications), PCT pilot by July 2001, merge pilots and releases into full EFS by late 2001–2003. Provide participation information via PTO Electronic Business Center.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFS / ePAVE security and submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic submissions use PTO 'submission engine' software (ePAVE) to identify submission type, electronic filer, and attach specification, claims, drawings; use PKI for transmission security and require digital certificates before transmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must obtain digital certificates/public-private keys from PTO before transmitting files. ePAVE automates combining files and digital signing/encryption. Specific pilots have phased rollout schedules (EFS BIO, limited-complexity utility pilot, PCT pilot, provisional and biotechnology submission pilots).

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal 3: Exceed customers' quality expectations through employee competencies and empowerment
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve customer satisfaction by enhancing competencies, empowerment, and service practices across patent processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement customer service offices, customer service training, in-process review system checking examiners' office actions, Patent Working Lab process improvements (relieve examiners of non-processing tasks), measure customer satisfaction via annual survey and key drivers, and establish quality-related programs and libraries to foster performance excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent customer satisfaction key drivers
rubrics_metrics.description: Four key drivers measured in the annual customer satisfaction survey: (1) Direct you promptly to the proper office or person; (2) Return telephone calls within one business day; (3) Set forth clearly in written communications the examiner's technical, procedural, and legal positions; (4) Conduct a thorough search during the patent examination process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY1999 improvements: driver 1 up 11%, driver 2 up 9%, driver 3 up 8%, driver 4 up 7%. Use these drivers to guide process changes and training; track via repeated surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrated Quality Management System (PTO Quality Council)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish an integrated quality management system including leadership and oversight through a Quality Council that sets policy on survey methodology, in-house assessments, and performance measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System outputs include periodic self-assessments, integration of performance measures, sharing best practices, fostering performance excellence, assisting business units with opportunities for improvement, establishing a performance excellence library, liaison for quality awards, and facilitating knowledge management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal 4: Assess fees commensurate with resource use and customer efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Set patent and trademark fees so collections are commensurate with business area resources and customer efficiency, using activity-based costing to guide adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public Law 106-113 adjusted fees (re-establishing USPTO and adjusting patent/trademark fees); some patent fees decreased while trademark fees may be increased above inflation to reach parity. Use fee policy to align revenues with expenses of business areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark timely processing target
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration decisions for trademark applications will be determined within thirteen months of filing; initial action (first-action) pendency goal is three months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY1999 performance: first action pendency decreased from 7.2 months (end FY1998) to 4.6 months (end FY1999), a 36% improvement. To reach the three-month goal, staffing increases (e.g., number of law offices and examining attorneys) and process changes are implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark quality legal examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of registrability must be accurately and clearly stated throughout the examination process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure examiners' communications clearly articulate technical, procedural, and legal positions; incorporate quality measures and in-process reviews to monitor clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of trademark products (notices and documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure trademark notices and products (filing receipts, Notice of Allowance, Notice of Abandonment, Certificates of Registration) contain correct information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement process improvements (scanning, TradeUps data capture, TRAM enhancements) and quality checks to reduce issuance of incorrect notices; track errors and address root causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective handling of trademark customer concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide only clear and accurate answers to customer questions regarding problems or delays in processing trademark applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign specific staff to solve problems and find root causes; use performance measures that assess quality from the customer's point of view and create manager-customer problem-solving partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Electronic Application System (e-TEAS) standards and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide electronic filing for trademarks via e-TEAS: 24/7 filing, payment by credit card or deposit account, immediate electronic confirmation with serial number, and filing date equal to date of receipt (regardless of business day).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E-TEAS reduces manual processing steps and makes initial processing one-third faster; rules for electronic filing were revised (e.g., modified signature requirements) to facilitate attorney filings. Encourage customers to file electronically and provide downloadable forms for those who must mail additional materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: TradeUps / TRAM / TARR / TESS modernization criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Modernize trademark data capture and processing: use TradeUps to code applications and add tagged data to TRAM, provide full scanned page images online, integrate e-TEAS electronic data, and replace TRAM with an open system enabling full electronic workflows. TARR provides public access to application/registration status; TESS scheduled to replace existing search engine with daily updates and examiner-like search capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phased enhancements: TradeUps II supports text editing, TradeUps automated interfaces eliminate initial paper review, TRAM changes to accommodate Treaty provisions delayed broader replacement; planned development of a trademark information system to replace paper and permit full electronic processing by 2000–2004 timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark customer satisfaction targets and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure overall customer satisfaction and target improvement (explicit FY1999 target: 80% customer satisfaction; actual overall increased from 63% in FY1998 to 69% in FY1999).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus FY2000 efforts on timeliness, handling delays and mistakes—identify internal processing issues and execute targeted improvements to reach the 80% target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing and hiring as performance levers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use hiring and staffing levels to meet processing and timeliness goals: examples include hiring 800 patent examiners in FY1999, hiring 136 trademark examining attorneys in 1999, increasing total trademark examining attorneys to 367 and planning to maintain staffing at 375.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruitment incentives (bonuses, higher step levels), support from HR, and aggressive recruitment campaigns are cited as methods to meet hiring goals. Staffing is explicitly linked to capacity to handle filing growth and meet cycle-time and pendency targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing adoption metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Track adoption and throughput of electronic filing systems: e-TEAS received more than 20,600 trademark applications (21,600 classes); electronic patent filing pilots (EFS BIO and limited-complexity utility pilot) have specific participation numbers and expansion timelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure benefits such as faster initial processing, immediate confirmations, reduction in manual steps, and scanning replacements. Encourage customers to adopt standardized electronic formats to improve throughput and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Independent Inventor Programs service standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a dedicated Office to meet the special needs of independent inventors and very small businesses, giving them a doorway at the PTO's highest policy levels to bring concerns and provide input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This program is a large-scale comprehensive approach to assist individual inventors (more than a quarter of PTO's customer base) and is considered a metric of customer outreach/service; monitor feedback/approval from the independent inventor community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work-at-Home pilot productivity criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Test remote work arrangements for examining attorneys to increase productivity (example: 18 attorneys worked from home three days a week resulting in significantly increased examination hours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pilot results to expand program (plan to expand to up to 60 examining attorneys) as an operational alternative to address increasing filings and limited office space; measure productivity changes and consider expansion based on outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and performance problem-resolution program
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop performance measures assessing quality from the customer's point of view and create programs with managers and customers working together to solve service problems and find root causes of delays and errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign specific staff to problem-solving and use customer satisfaction surveys and operational metrics to prioritize and track improvements; address four trademark-specific goals (quality legal examination; timely processing; accuracy of products; effective customer handling).
